name: Pegboy
label: Quarterstick (Touch and Go)
lede: John Haggerty walked out of Naked Raygun, grabbed his little brother and two guys from the Bhopal Stiffs, and gave Touch and Go's new sister label its very first record. Steve Albini once filled in on bass.

hero.by: Pegboy at the Cobra Lounge, Chicago, August 27, 2011. Photo: Robman94, Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Out of the Stiffs and the Raygun
eras.text: Pegboy is a Chicago punk family tree in one band: a guitarist from Naked Raygun, a drummer from The Effigies, and the singer and bassist of the Bhopal Stiffs. The first record came out in 1990 on a label that didn't exist a few months earlier.

years.h: The Bhopal Stiffs cut a ten-song demo at CRC
years.p: [[Larry Damore|bf5f789e-c6f4-4a5d-bf61-69000e413d4d]] and Steve Saylors's hardcore band records at Chicago Recording Company with Iain Burgess. Pegboy's Wikipedia page credits John Haggerty as producer.

years.src: Wikipedia: Naked Raygun · Wikipedia: Bhopal Stiffs · Newcity Music
years.h: John Haggerty quits Naked Raygun to start a band with his brother
years.p: Haggerty, Raygun's guitarist since 1983, wants to play with Joe Haggerty, drummer in the Effigies and Bloodsport. The Bhopal Stiffs split the same year.
years.xp: The Stiffs' drummer Dave Schleitwiler didn't come along: Haggerty wanted his brother on drums, says the Bhopal Stiffs' Wikipedia page. Damore and Saylors did.

yt: Pegboy live on WZRD Chicago, July 26, 1990
years.h: A live set on Chicago radio station WZRD
years.p: The new band plays the radio a month after recording its first EP.

years.src: Wikipedia: Three-Chord Monte · Wikipedia: Quarterstick Records
yt: Live at Cabaret Metro, Chicago, May 26, 1991
years.h: Three-Chord Monte is Quarterstick's first release
years.p: Four songs, 14 minutes, recorded with Iain Burgess at Bombadier Beetle Studios in June. Quarterstick is Touch and Go's new sister label, founded that year.

eras.title: 120 Minutes, then a bass player shortage
eras.text: Strong Reaction made Pegboy one of the city's great hopes and put them on MTV. Then their bassist went back to work, and the replacements were a D.C. post-hardcore guitarist and the most famous engineer in Chicago.

yt: 'Through My Fingers' on MTV 120 Minutes, May 12, 1991
years.h: Pegboy turns up on MTV's 120 Minutes
years.p: Host Dave Kendall plays 'Through My Fingers', the opener of Three-Chord Monte.

years.h: Strong Reaction: 27 minutes recorded at CRC
years.p: Burgess produces again. The Chicago Tribune's Greg Kot hears anthemic choruses in the tradition of Haggerty's old band.
years.xp: The A.V. Club, looking back, wrote that it "has aged with a rugged grace that puts most of its contemporaries to shame." Trouser Press said any quibbles "are obliterated by the ferocious attack."

years.h: Saylors's job keeps him home; J. Robbins plays the Social Distortion tour
years.p: Steve Saylors can't tour around work and leaves. [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]] of [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]] fills in on bass for a tour with [[Social Distortion|e1e05cce-3922-44e1-8f20-015abe5e309d]].

years.h: Steve Albini plays bass, and engineers, on Fore
years.p: Four songs cut at Westonworld in Chicago in June. [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]], a longtime friend of the band, fills the bass slot for the EP.

eras.title: Kezdy on bass, Burgess in France
eras.text: With Pierre Kezdy, Naked Raygun's old bassist, the line-up settled for 13 years. The band recorded in the French countryside, toured with the Jesus Lizard, covered Cheap Trick, and then announced that New Year's Eve 1999 would be the end.

years.cap: Poster for the Jesus Lizard, Pegboy and Kepone at the Commodore, Vancouver, November 30, 1994
years.h: Pierre Kezdy, ex-Naked Raygun, becomes the permanent bassist
years.p: [[Pierre Kezdy|061ef98c-497e-4a61-9464-10bf622c3c24]] played with Haggerty in Raygun until 1989; Raygun itself had split in 1992.

yt: Live at First Avenue, Minneapolis, October 6, 1994
years.h: Earwig is cut at Iain Burgess's Blackbox in rural France
years.p: Recorded in April in Noyant-la-Gravoyère, with a cover of [[Mission of Burma|db9d25d7-a85b-4a29-b2ff-8f5b69ed691e]]'s 'Revolver'. The Washington Post picked 'You' and 'Blister' as the "potent merger of pop and wallop."

yt: Live at Liberty Lunch, Austin, December 17, 1994
years.h: Three Touch and Go bands close a tour in Austin
years.p: Pegboy, [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]] and Kepone finish their autumn run at Liberty Lunch. The Austin American-Statesman calls it industrial-strength noise from the North.

years.h: A split single with Kepone, called Dangermare
years.p: Quarterstick pairs Pegboy with Kepone, its tourmates from 1994.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cha Cha Damore · Wikipedia: Pegboy · Razorcake
years.h: Albini produces Cha Cha Damore, Cheap Trick cover included
years.p: Eleven songs in 29 minutes, ending with Rick Nielsen's 'Surrender'. The Chicago Reader called it the band's best.
years.xp: Kezdy was blunt about it to the Fort Worth Star-Telegram: "Yeah it's just another Pegboy record." A few months later he told Flipside why he did it: "It's a release. I write a song and I play it live and people like it."

q: And you know what I've learned? Not a goddamn thing.
yt: Live at the Fireside Bowl, Chicago, June 5, 1998
years.h: Flipside catches Pegboy in Atlanta
years.p: Damore, at the Point, on what 17 years in punk rock had taught him. He also gave the band's touring rule: have fun first.
years.xp: Sean Carswell's interview ran in Flipside #112. Damore's description of how the band works live: "Our band is like a parasite. If you feed off each other and get that going, it's cool."

years.h: A "farewell" show on New Year's Eve
years.p: The Chicago Tribune runs the story the same day. A few years later the band denies it was ever really a farewell.

eras.title: Not really goodbye
eras.text: Pegboy drifted back into clubs, Chicago's punk bands kept turning up to honor them, and Naked Raygun eventually took Kezdy back. The band settled into a rhythm: practice once a week, play when it feels right.

years.h: Back to doing what they love, says the Tribune
years.p: The paper's April 12 piece has Pegboy playing live again, two years after the farewell.

years.h: Matt Skiba and Vic Bondi sing Pegboy at a tribute show
years.p: Matt Skiba of [[Alkaline Trio|69421e11-e4c3-4854-951b-ceab4972e38e]] and [[Vic Bondi|3761c6de-75f8-4c9b-931e-fd6a593594a0]] of Articles of Faith play a Pegboy tribute night, and Underground Communique releases The World I Know: A Tribute to Pegboy.
years.xp: The fan list on Wikipedia runs to [[Rise Against|606bf117-494f-4864-891f-09d63ff6aa4b]]'s Tim McIlrath, Hot Water Music's Chuck Ragan and Shai Hulud's Matt Fox too. Pegboy's own influences, they've said, run from [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]] and [[Dag Nasty|4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192]] to [[Buzzcocks|31e9c35b-2675-4632-8596-f9bd9286f6c8]], [[The Replacements|dc0d05ce-2f47-4962-b4fa-8631a0a51987]] and [[Hüsker Dü|5c4c90a4-539f-4101-83cf-301bc6a94e06]].

years.h: A Riot Fest reunion
years.p: Newcity dates the band's return to Riot Fest 2006, the same festival that brought Naked Raygun back.

years.cap: Pegboy in Chicago on the Touch and Go 25th weekend, September 9, 2006
years.h: On the bill for Touch and Go's 25th birthday
years.p: Pegboy plays the label's anniversary weekend at Chicago's Hideout.

years.h: Kezdy goes back to Naked Raygun; "Skinny" Mike Thompson in
years.p: Kezdy rejoins the reunited Raygun, and Mike Thompson takes over on bass.

years.cap: Pegboy at the Cobra Lounge, August 2011
years.h: A night at the Cobra Lounge, and a fly-rod company
years.p: Pegboy plays Chicago's Cobra Lounge. That year Damore starts Flying Pig Fly Rods, making and selling casting rods.
years.xp: Razorcake's update on the band: Joe Haggerty turned his garage into a woodshop around 2007, and John Haggerty has filled in for [[Stiff Little Fingers|022865bc-84c9-4002-b6c1-d5fc6e12b7d8]] and plays with Jake Burns in the Nefarious Fat Cats, whose holiday shows at the Liar's Club raise money for a children's charity.

eras.title: Thirty years, two goodbyes
eras.text: In October 2020, a week after Pierre Kezdy died, Newcity marked Pegboy's 30 years. Four years later the friend who'd played bass on Fore was gone too, and the band was still playing Riot Fest.

years.h: Pierre Kezdy dies of cancer at 58
years.p: The bassist on Earwig and Cha Cha Damore, and Naked Raygun's bassist from 1985, dies in Glenview, Illinois. Newcity's 30th-anniversary tribute to Pegboy runs a week later.

years.h: Herb Rosen takes over the bass
years.p: Thompson's 15 years end, and Rosen becomes Pegboy's sixth bassist.

years.h: Steve Albini, Fore's bassist, dies at 61
years.p: Albini, who also produced Cha Cha Damore, has a heart attack at home in Chicago.

yt: Field of Darkness, live at Riot Fest, September 21, 2025
years.h: 'Field of Darkness' at Riot Fest, 34 years on
years.p: Pegboy plays the Chicago festival again, with the Strong Reaction single in the set.
